articles.summary: A vulnerability in the Cursor IDE on Windows allows malicious repositories to automatically execute a local 'git.exe' file without user interaction or warning, potentially exposing sensitive data and credentials. The flaw triggers execution immediately upon opening a repository and persists as long as the project remains open.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds SonicWall and Microsoft flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include specific security flaws discovered in SonicWall and Microsoft products. These additions follow reports of active exploitation of these vulnerabilities in the wild.

articles.title: ClickFix is changing the economics of social engineering
articles.summary: ClickFix is an emerging social engineering technique that bypasses traditional security tools by manipulating users into manually executing malicious commands via system dialogs. This method has evolved into an industrialized attack ecosystem that avoids exploits and vulnerabilities, posing a significant challenge to endpoint defense systems.

articles.title: AI-driven bug hunting fuels record Microsoft Patch Tuesday
articles.summary: Microsoft addressed over 570 vulnerabilities in its July 2026 Patch Tuesday, including two actively exploited flaws and a new zero-day elevation of privilege vulnerability dubbed 'LegacyHive' disclosed by researchers.

articles.title: TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 provides a technical analysis of TuxBot v3, an evolving IoT botnet framework that leverages LLMs for development. The report details the malware's cross-compiled binaries, command-and-control infrastructure, and existing security flaws.

articles.title: Compromised AsyncAPI npm Packages Deliver Multi-Stage Botnet Malware
articles.summary: Four npm packages within the @asyncapi namespace were compromised to distribute a multi-stage botnet loader. Security researchers identified multiple versions of these packages as malicious, posing a significant supply chain threat.

articles.title: AWS retools Security Hub for AI and multicloud threats
articles.summary: AWS has updated its Security Hub to include AI workload protection and cross-cloud monitoring, starting with Microsoft Azure support to improve threat prioritization. The expansion aims to accelerate incident response by consolidating security findings across multicloud environments.

articles.title: FreeRDP 3.29.0 security update resolves 22 advisories
articles.summary: FreeRDP has released version 3.29.0, a security update that addresses 22 advisories through hardening measures and improved bounds checking across its codebase.

articles.title: SonicWall warns of active exploitation of two SMA 1000 zero-days
articles.summary: SonicWall has issued an urgent warning regarding the active exploitation of two zero-day vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 series appliances, one of which allows for arbitrary command execution. The company is actively investigating incidents linked to these flaws and advises immediate action.

articles.title: Fortinet adds AI controls and data loss prevention to FortiEndpoint
articles.summary: Fortinet has updated its FortiEndpoint platform to include new AI controls, data loss prevention features, and risk-scoring capabilities to help organizations manage sensitive data and AI usage securely. These enhancements aim to simplify security operations and improve threat visibility across distributed environments.

articles.title: Product showcase: Trust Chain TPRM turns vendor compliance evidence into verified assurance
articles.summary: Strike Graph has launched Trust Chain, an AI-powered third-party risk management solution that replaces traditional security questionnaires with automated, evidence-based compliance verification. By using AI to evaluate vendor documentation against specific requirements, it shifts from self-reported attestations to verifiable security assurance.

articles.title: SingGuard-NSFA: Open-source guardrails for agentic AI
articles.summary: SingGuard-NSFA is a new open-source guardrail framework designed to mitigate operational threats in agentic AI workflows using a taxonomy based on the CIA triad. The project offers four model sizes built on Qwen3.5 to address risks like prompt injection.

articles.title: Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days Exploited, One Could Enable Admin Commands
articles.summary: SonicWall has issued a warning regarding two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 series appliances, including a critical-rated flaw that allows for arbitrary command execution.

articles.title: The MDR renewal question: What changes when AI can handle the alerts
articles.summary: As AI-driven automation improves alert handling, security leaders are re-evaluating the value and necessity of traditional managed detection and response (MDR) service renewals. The shift suggests that internal teams may increasingly rely on AI to address alert fatigue, potentially reducing the reliance on outsourced security providers.

articles.title: An AI overthinking attack can tie a robot up for over a minute
articles.summary: Researchers at Michigan Technological University have discovered an 'overthinking' attack that exploits vision-language models in robots, causing them to stall for over a minute by flooding their input with specific text. This vulnerability targets the way robots interpret visual data, potentially disrupting their autonomous operations.

articles.title: AI used to help plan the break-in, now it’s doing the break-in
articles.summary: Recent findings reveal that cyber attackers are increasingly using autonomous AI to execute full-scale exploitation workflows without human intervention. By bypassing safety controls in AI models, threat actors are automating complex attack chains.

articles.title: White House details ‘Gold Eagle’ clearinghouse for AI cyber threats
articles.summary: The White House has launched 'Gold Eagle,' a new intelligence clearinghouse designed to track vulnerabilities in AI systems and accelerate the prioritization of security patches. This initiative serves as a central hub for sharing actionable threat intelligence to bolster the nation's AI infrastructure.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday security updates for July 2026, the largest update ever. 621 CVEs in one month
articles.summary: Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday sets a record with 621 addressed CVEs, including two actively exploited zero-days and critical vulnerabilities in key infrastructure services. This represents the largest single-month security update in the company's history.

articles.title: Patchpocalypse Now: Microsoft tops last month's record with 622 Patch Tuesday CVEs
articles.summary: Microsoft has set a new record for Patch Tuesday, addressing 622 vulnerabilities in a single month. This massive volume of patches follows a previously record-breaking month of 206 CVEs, highlighting a significant surge in identified security flaws.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Record 622 Flaws, Including Two Zero-Days Under Active Attack
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a record-breaking set of security updates addressing 622 vulnerabilities, including two zero-day flaws that are currently being actively exploited. Users are urged to prioritize these fixes immediately due to the active nature of the threats.

articles.title: Microsoft discloses ‘the mother of all’ vulnerability loads, tripling June’s previous record
articles.summary: Microsoft has reported a record-breaking surge in vulnerability disclosures, tripling the figures from June and validating predictions that AI-driven discovery would significantly accelerate the identification of software flaws. The report highlights an exponential increase in identified defects, prompting urgent warnings for security teams to bolster their patching efforts.

articles.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions VPN Provider and Cryptor Seller Behind Billions in Ransomware Losses
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned a VPN provider and a cryptor seller for facilitating ransomware operations that caused billions in losses. These sanctions target the infrastructure and tooling enabling global cybercriminal activities against critical infrastructure.

articles.title: US unseals indictment against alleged operators of Russian bulletproof hosting service
articles.summary: U.S. authorities have unsealed an indictment against the operators of a Russian bulletproof hosting service accused of supporting cybercriminal activities. The operation involved two companies based in St. Petersburg that provided infrastructure and technical assistance for illegal operations.

articles.title: SAP Patches CVSS 9.9 NetWeaver ABAP Flaw That Could Expose or Modify Data
articles.summary: SAP has released a patch for CVE-2026-44747, a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the NetWeaver Application Server ABAP that allows authenticated attackers to corrupt memory and compromise data.

articles.title: SonicWall SMA appliances targeted in zero-day attacks (CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410)
articles.summary: SonicWall has released patches for two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 Series appliances and advises users to check for compromises, reset credentials, and re-deploy affected systems.

articles.title: Upwind Finds Coordinated Supply Chain Campaign Compromising Multiple AsyncAPI npm Packages
articles.summary: Upwind has identified a coordinated supply chain attack that successfully compromised several AsyncAPI npm packages. The campaign spanned multiple vectors, including developer systems and publishing pipelines, posing a significant risk to the software supply chain.

articles.title: Finland issues wanted notice for hacker behind massive psychotherapy data breach
articles.summary: Finnish authorities have issued a wanted notice for Julius Kivimäki, the primary suspect in the massive 2020 Vastaamo psychotherapy clinic data breach. His current location remains unknown, though his legal counsel suggests he is likely outside of Finland.

articles.title: Researchers Say Claude for Chrome Flaw Lets Rogue Extensions Trigger Gmail Reads
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in the Claude for Chrome extension allows malicious third-party browser extensions to exploit existing sessions and access sensitive user data from Gmail, Google Docs, and Calendar. The flaw functions by executing scripts on claude.ai to trigger unauthorized tasks via the extension.

articles.title: LabubaRAT Masquerades as NVIDIA Software to Control Windows Hosts
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a new Rust-based remote access trojan called LabubaRAT that disguises itself as legitimate NVIDIA software to gain persistent control over Windows hosts. The malware enables attackers to profile compromised systems and perform unauthorized hands-on activity.

articles.title: Tego AI Finds Claude Tag Slack Integration Can Trigger Unauthorized Enterprise Actions
articles.summary: Security researchers at Tego AI have discovered a vulnerability in the Claude Slack integration that allows unauthorized execution of enterprise actions. This flaw poses a significant risk to organizational data integrity and automated workflows.

articles.title: Welsh Doxbin admin jailed for egging on swatters from behind a screen
articles.summary: Callum Dare, an administrator of the Doxbin website, was sentenced to prison for inciting individuals to conduct dangerous swatting hoaxes and creating content from the resulting footage.

articles.title: Treasury sanctions First VPN Service, others for abetting ransomware gangs
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned a VPN service and two individuals accused of facilitating ransomware operations by providing infrastructure and obfuscation tools. This action aims to disrupt the digital ecosystem supporting cybercriminal syndicates.

articles.title: NATO logistics, Ukrainian troops are top subjects of Russian camera hacks, advisory says
articles.summary: Dutch intelligence officials have warned that Russian operatives are compromising internet-connected cameras across Europe to surveil NATO logistics and Ukrainian military personnel. This espionage campaign highlights a persistent effort to use unsecured IoT devices for strategic intelligence gathering.

articles.title: RabbitMQ Flaws Could Leak OAuth Secrets and Expose Cross-Tenant Queue Metadata
articles.summary: Researchers discovered two access control vulnerabilities in the RabbitMQ message broker that allow unauthorized access to OAuth secrets and cross-tenant queue metadata. These flaws could potentially lead to full system takeover and tenant boundary bypasses.

articles.title: New macOS malware steals passwords by posing as Apple’s crash-reporting tool
articles.summary: Jamf Threat Labs discovered a new macOS infostealer called CrashStealer that masquerades as a legitimate Apple crash-reporting tool to exfiltrate passwords, Keychain data, and cryptocurrency assets. The malware has evolved from its development phase in May to active in-the-wild exploitation as of July.

articles.title: Download: The ultimate guide to network operations management
articles.summary: This guide addresses the inefficiencies and operational bottlenecks in modern network management caused by manual workflows. It proposes the adoption of intelligent workflows to improve IT and security team collaboration and visibility.

articles.title: 11 Old Microsoft-Signed Linux UEFI Shims Could Let Attackers Bypass Secure Boot
articles.summary: Eleven legacy, Microsoft-signed UEFI shims have been identified as vulnerable, potentially allowing attackers to bypass Secure Boot and execute malicious code at the boot level. This vulnerability poses a significant risk as it could facilitate the deployment of persistent UEFI bootkits.

articles.title: Musk promises purge after Grok Build caught sending entire repos to the cloud
articles.summary: xAI's Grok AI tool was found to be inadvertently uploading entire code repositories to the cloud, prompting Elon Musk to promise a purge of the system. Although the data leaks have ceased, researchers indicate that the implemented privacy commands were not the actual cause of the resolution.

articles.title: “Context bombs” can frustrate AI-driven attacks, researchers found
articles.summary: Researchers at Tracebit have developed 'context bombs,' a defensive technique using decoy resources to detect and frustrate AI-driven cyberattacks by providing early alerts.

articles.title: 'The bots are alive!' Jailbroken Gemini spun up new C2 server for Russian fraudster in just 6 minutes
articles.summary: A jailbroken version of Google's Gemini AI was used to rapidly deploy a command-and-control server for a Russian cybercriminal, demonstrating the growing efficiency of AI-assisted malicious infrastructure setup.

articles.title: Telegram’s t.me Links Go Offline After Registry Places Domain on serverHold
articles.summary: Telegram's t.me links became inaccessible after the .ME domain registry applied a 'serverHold' status, though the underlying messaging application remains functional. The specific reason for the registry's intervention has not been publicly disclosed.

articles.title: Study of 85 Crypto Wallet Extensions Finds Address Leaks and Cross-Site Tracking Risks
articles.summary: A study of 85 popular browser-based crypto wallet extensions revealed privacy vulnerabilities that allow third parties to link user addresses and track browsing behavior across different websites. These leaks pose significant risks to user anonymity by enabling the correlation of separate wallet addresses and online identities.

articles.title: How Pentera Turns AI Security Workflows into Validation Engines
articles.summary: Pentera leverages AI to consolidate fragmented security signals into actionable validation engines, allowing teams to move beyond static risk scoring. This approach aims to provide a more holistic view of the attack surface to better counter evolving threats.

articles.title: OAuth Client ID Spoofing Lets Attackers Validate Stolen Microsoft Entra Credentials
articles.summary: Threat actors are using a novel OAuth client ID spoofing technique to validate stolen Microsoft Entra credentials without triggering standard sign-in alerts. This evasion method allows attackers to enumerate accounts and verify compromised credentials while bypassing existing security telemetry.

articles.title: Baddies caught exploiting extensions bugs with perfect 10 scores on vulnerable Joomla websites
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting high-severity vulnerabilities with perfect CVSS scores in Joomla extensions, specifically iCagenda and Balbooa Forms. These flaws pose a significant risk to the large number of websites relying on the Joomla CMS.

articles.title: Google adds FIDO2 keys and phone passkeys to Windows login via GCPW
articles.summary: Google has updated its Google Credential Provider for Windows (GCPW) to support FIDO2 security keys and phone passkeys for 2-step verification. This enhancement allows organizations to strengthen Windows login security by utilizing phishing-resistant hardware authentication.

articles.title: No one knows how many old shims can still bypass UEFI Secure Boot
articles.summary: ESET researchers discovered that outdated UEFI shims, which are signed by Microsoft to facilitate Linux boot processes, contain vulnerabilities that allow attackers to bypass Secure Boot protections. Because the full extent of vulnerable, signed shims in the ecosystem remains unknown, these security bypasses pose a significant long-term risk.

articles.title: Attacker Used AI to Build Custom PowerShell Recon Malware
articles.summary: Huntress analysts identified a malicious PowerShell script generated by AI used for Active Directory reconnaissance, highlighting an emerging trend of attackers leveraging artificial intelligence to develop evasive tools. The discovery occurred during an incident response investigation on a compromised Windows server.

articles.title: Millions of Microsoft Entra Accounts Targeted in OAuth Client ID Spoofing Campaigns
articles.summary: Attackers are utilizing OAuth client ID spoofing to bypass sign-in detections and compromise Microsoft Entra accounts at scale. This technique allows threat actors to perform credential testing while evading standard security monitoring.

articles.title: UK charges five persons linked to fraud platform behind more than a million scam calls
articles.summary: The UK's National Crime Agency has charged five London residents for their involvement in 'Russian Coms,' a caller ID spoofing platform responsible for facilitating over a million fraudulent scam calls.

articles.title: Malware Hits Japan’s Largest Taxi Company Nihon Kotsu, Services Temporarily Suspended
articles.summary: Nihon Kotsu, Japan’s largest taxi company, suspended dispatch and booking services after a malware-driven unauthorized access event forced a system-wide shutdown.

articles.title: Grok Build Uploads Entire Git Repositories to xAI Storage, Not Just Files It Reads
articles.summary: xAI's Grok Build CLI was found to be exfiltrating entire Git repositories, including sensitive commit histories, to cloud storage without authorization beyond the scope of its assigned tasks.

articles.title: Microsoft Entra ID authentication overhaul to start in September 2026
articles.summary: Microsoft is transitioning Entra ID authentication to passkeys as the default method, replacing legacy SMS and voice-based MFA by early 2027 to improve account security.

articles.title: U.S. Sanctions First VPN Service and Malware Cryptor Seller Over Ransomware Support
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury has sanctioned a VPN provider and two individuals for facilitating ransomware attacks by supporting cybercriminal operations. This marks a significant move to disrupt the infrastructure that enables illicit digital activities.

articles.title: CrashStealer: New macOS Infostealer Uses Signed Apps to Evade Gatekeeper
articles.summary: The newly discovered macOS infostealer CrashStealer bypasses Gatekeeper protections by utilizing signed applications to exfiltrate credentials and crypto-wallets. The malware has progressed from development to active deployment as of July 2026.

articles.title: Greenhat Announces Successful Delegation at Web Summit Vancouver 2026
articles.summary: Greenhat successfully conducted a delegation event at the Web Summit Vancouver 2026. This announcement highlights corporate engagement within the cybersecurity community.

articles.title: 148 npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet
articles.summary: Researchers discovered 148 malicious npm packages disguised as student proxy tools that infected browsers to participate in a DDoS botnet for two weeks in May. The campaign leveraged the npm registry to host harmful code, specifically targeting end-users visiting student-focused proxy sites.

articles.title: New tutorials on underground hacking forums have roughly doubled
articles.summary: Recent data reveals a twofold increase in unique, original hacking and financial fraud tutorials appearing on underground forums, with a specific focus on payment card theft and cash-out schemes. This shift indicates a growing sophistication in the educational resources available to cybercriminals.

articles.title: Microsoft Maps Year-Long ShinyHunters-Linked Salesforce Data Theft Across Three Paths
articles.summary: The ShinyHunters threat group has spent a year exfiltrating data from corporate Salesforce environments by exploiting trusted third-party OAuth connections rather than software vulnerabilities. This campaign highlights a systemic risk in how organizations manage application-to-application trust permissions.

articles.title: The best defense against AI attacks turns out to be a skeptical human
articles.summary: The 2026 SANS AI Survey reveals that while generative AI adoption in cybersecurity has reached 78%, reliability remains a major issue, underscoring the critical need for human oversight to counter AI-driven threats.

articles.title: Fake smart home residents could stand in for real ones in security research
articles.summary: Researchers from Leipzig University and ipoque have developed a method using synthetic data to simulate smart home user behavior, overcoming the limitations of acquiring real-world usage data for security testing. This approach could significantly accelerate the development and robustness of smart home security solutions.

articles.title: Your vendor’s vendor might be the real breach risk
articles.summary: The article warns that supply chain attacks are evolving, as threat actors target third-party subcontractors to gain unauthorized access to primary organizations' systems via unvetted credentials. This emphasizes the need for broader visibility into the security posture of an organization's entire vendor ecosystem.

articles.title: Chatto: Open-source team messenger with privacy at its core
articles.summary: Chatto has released an open-source, self-hosted team messaging platform designed to give organizations full control over their communication data by hosting it on their own infrastructure. This solution offers a privacy-focused alternative to commercial messaging services with a simplified single-executable installation process.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: July 14, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security lists current job openings for cybersecurity professionals, including a position for a Cyber Network Engineer at Fiserv. The post highlights the ongoing demand for experts to manage enterprise network security and cloud infrastructure.

articles.title: Hackers steal Lidl customer data from external service provider
articles.summary: Hackers breached a third-party service provider to access and exfiltrate a database containing customer information for Lidl. The incident was limited to external files and did not impact the company's primary online shopping platform.

articles.title: States are building their own election defense networks as federal support evaporates
articles.summary: State election officials are increasingly establishing independent cybersecurity defense networks due to a lack of trust in federal directives and declining support. This shift reflects growing friction between local election administration and federal oversight.

articles.title: EU leaders eye social media ban for children under age 13
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed a potential ban on social media access for children under the age of 13 to improve online safety. This initiative reflects growing regulatory consensus regarding the protection of minors in the digital landscape.

articles.title: Lidl Notified Online Shop Customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands of a Data Breach
articles.summary: Lidl informed online customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that their personal data was compromised following a security incident at a third-party IT service provider. The company confirmed that customer payment information was not affected by the breach.

articles.title: VPN service favored by ransomware groups is sanctioned by US
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury has sanctioned First VPN Service and its administrator for facilitating ransomware operations, alongside a Belarusian individual linked to malware development.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a Cisco IOS flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has officially added CVE-2008-4128, a CSRF vulnerability affecting Cisco IOS 12.4 on Cisco 871 routers, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

articles.title: CrashStealer macOS Malware Uses Notarized Dropper to Pass Gatekeeper Checks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a new macOS information stealer called CrashStealer that utilizes a notarized dropper to bypass Apple's Gatekeeper security checks. The malware is written in native C++ and performs local password validation to exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems.

articles.title: Google and Microsoft Pull ModHeader With 1.6 Million Installs After Dormant Collector Found
articles.summary: Google and Microsoft removed the popular ModHeader extension from their stores after discovering a hidden, dormant browsing-history collector. While the malicious feature was inactive and no data exfiltration was confirmed, the extension was pulled as a proactive security measure.

articles.title: Russian celebrity journalist Ksenia Sobchak says hackers accessed Telegram channels via email breach
articles.summary: Russian journalist Ksenia Sobchak reported that her Telegram channels were compromised through an email-based breach, resulting in the unauthorized release of potentially fabricated private correspondence. The incident highlights the risks associated with account takeovers involving linked third-party email services.

articles.title: Hackers breach Lidl’s IT service provider, steal customer data
articles.summary: Lidl notified customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that their personal data was stolen after an unidentified group breached one of the supermarket chain's IT service providers. The company confirmed that a specific file containing customer information was briefly accessed and exfiltrated.

articles.title: Europe strikes out against Russia’s Turla over espionage, ‘destructive attacks’
articles.summary: The EU and U.K. have issued sanctions and formal attribution against Russian FSB officials for orchestrating espionage campaigns and destructive cyberattacks, including strikes against Poland’s energy grid.

articles.title: EU and UK officially blame Russian spies for cyberattack on Poland's power grid
articles.summary: The EU and UK have formally attributed a cyberattack on Poland's power grid to Russian state-sponsored actors, resulting in coordinated international sanctions. The incident, which occurred during winter, threatened to disrupt energy services for half a million citizens.

articles.title: Officials once again warn defenders that Russian hackers are targeting network devices
articles.summary: State-sponsored Russian hackers are actively targeting network infrastructure across multiple critical sectors, prompting renewed security warnings for organizations. The campaign focuses on compromising essential services including energy, finance, and government systems.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: ShareFile Threat, Citrix Bleed 2 Ransomware, AI Coding Attacks, and More
articles.summary: This week's security landscape highlights ongoing risks from Citrix and ShareFile vulnerabilities, while noting the accelerating threat of AI-driven cyberattacks. Organizations are struggling to keep pace with patching cycles as attackers increasingly leverage automation to exploit unpatched flaws.

articles.title: EU and UK blacklist Russia’s cyber operators over efforts to destabilize Europe
articles.summary: The EU and UK have imposed joint sanctions on dozens of Russian individuals and entities, alleging they are part of a malicious cyber ecosystem designed to destabilize European nations. The measures target state-linked actors, hacktivists, and private companies involved in cyber operations against international partners.

articles.title: Torq and Criminal IP Partner to Deliver Decision-Ready Threat Intelligence for Autonomous SOC Operations
articles.summary: Torq and Criminal IP have announced a partnership to integrate threat intelligence into autonomous Security Operations Center (SOC) workflows. This collaboration aims to provide automated, decision-ready data to improve security response efficiency.

articles.title: New MemGhost Attack Plants Persistent False Memories in AI Agents Through One Email
articles.summary: The MemGhost attack exploits AI agents by injecting malicious, persistent false memories through a single email, allowing attackers to manipulate the assistant's future behavior and responses. This technique enables subtle, stealthy tampering that persists across sessions without alerting the user.

articles.title: Tidal Cyber connects assets, vulnerabilities, and threats through Threat-Led Defense
articles.summary: Tidal Cyber has expanded its Threat-Led Defense platform to integrate asset visibility and vulnerability prioritization based on real-world adversary behavior. This shift focuses on an execution-centric model that links threats, assets, and vulnerabilities to improve defensive strategies.

articles.title: Cloudflare Precursor uses continuous behavioral analysis to stop advanced bots
articles.summary: Cloudflare has launched Precursor, a behavioral analysis engine that monitors user sessions in real time to identify and block sophisticated bot traffic. This tool aims to improve bot detection precision while eliminating the need for intrusive CAPTCHAs.

articles.title: Lumen expands managed detection and response with Cortex XSIAM integration
articles.summary: Lumen Technologies has launched its Defender Advanced Managed Detection and Response (AMDR) service by integrating Palo Alto Networks' Cortex XSIAM platform. This collaboration combines Lumen's network-embedded threat intelligence with AI-driven security operations to help enterprises improve incident response efficiency.

articles.title: Forg365 PhaaS Targets Microsoft 365 with Device Code and AitM Session Theft
articles.summary: Forg365 is a newly identified phishing-as-a-service platform that utilizes AI-enhanced lures, AitM, and device code phishing to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The service is actively marketed on Telegram for a recurring subscription fee.

articles.title: EU Targets FSB-Linked Hackers in New Sanctions Over Cyber Sabotage
articles.summary: The European Union has imposed sanctions on nine individuals and four entities linked to a Russian FSB-backed cyberespionage campaign that has targeted critical infrastructure since 2010.

articles.title: Ransomware negotiator who betrayed clients sentenced to 70 months in prison
articles.summary: A former ransomware negotiator has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for leaking confidential client data to the BlackCat ransomware group and participating in subsequent attacks. The individual exploited his position at an incident response firm to provide attackers with sensitive victim information and negotiating leverage.

articles.title: Fake OAuth client IDs are helping attackers slip past sign-in logs
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting a gap in Microsoft Entra ID by spoofing OAuth client IDs to perform account enumeration while evading standard sign-in telemetry logs.

articles.title: World Cup grudge attackers may have scored Argentine FA access via year-old infostealer infection
articles.summary: Hackers linked to the World Cup gained unauthorized access to the Argentine Football Association's systems by exploiting credentials stolen via a year-old infostealer infection. The breach highlights the long-term risk posed by dormant malware infections on corporate devices.

articles.title: Meta Files Patent for AI That Can Listen All Day and Track How You're Feeling
articles.summary: Meta has filed a patent for an AI system designed to continuously record audio, analyze emotional states, and log location and behavioral metadata. This raises significant privacy and surveillance concerns regarding user data collection and tracking.

articles.title: Security threat prompts Progress to disable ShareFile accounts, tell customers to shut down servers
articles.summary: Progress Software has directed customers to shut down their on-premises ShareFile Storage Zone Controllers due to a credible external security threat. As a precautionary measure, the company has disabled affected ShareFile accounts.

articles.title: Thinking Fast and Slow in the SOC: The Case for Combining Autonomous AI with Analyst Copilots
articles.summary: The article explores the integration of autonomous AI agents and analyst copilots in Security Operations Centers, emphasizing the need for a hybrid approach to optimize incident investigation. It highlights a real-world case study where a major enterprise is balancing these technologies to enhance detection efficiency.

articles.title: Siggen Backdoor Hits Windows Developers Via Infected Visual Studio Projects
articles.summary: The Siggen backdoor targets Windows developers by infecting Visual Studio projects to distribute malware, leveraging Steam for command-and-control communication and exfiltrating sensitive credentials and cryptocurrency data.

articles.title: Attacker Uses Suspected AI-Generated PowerShell Script to Map Active Directory
articles.summary: An unidentified threat actor utilized a suspected AI-generated PowerShell script to enumerate Active Directory components and exfiltrate sensitive network data. The incident highlights the growing risk of automated tools being leveraged for sophisticated reconnaissance and malicious reporting.

articles.title: Progress orders emergency ShareFile server shutdown over mystery security threat
articles.summary: Progress Software has directed ShareFile customers to shut down their servers immediately due to an unidentified security threat, despite stating there is currently no evidence of a data breach. The company is taking this proactive measure while it continues to investigate the potential vulnerability.

articles.title: FastNetMon eliminates third-party bgp lookups with Netomics
articles.summary: FastNetMon has launched Netomics, a self-hosted BGP routing intelligence platform that allows network operators to analyze global routing data without using third-party lookups. The tool integrates RPKI validation, routing history, and AI-assisted querying to improve network visibility and efficiency.

articles.title: Dutch Nationals Suspected in Odido Hack That Exposed Six Million Customers
articles.summary: Dutch police are seeking public assistance to identify local suspects behind a February 2026 phishing attack on telecom provider Odido that compromised the data of six million customers.

articles.title: Claude Code users keep 50% higher limits until July 19
articles.summary: Anthropic has extended a promotional 50% increase to weekly usage limits for Claude Code for eligible paid subscribers until July 19, 2026. This extension does not impact standard billing or service plans for users.

articles.title: AI-generated code has made security debt a governance problem
articles.summary: The rapid adoption of AI-generated code is exacerbating security debt, forcing CISOs to transition from simple tool approvals to comprehensive governance frameworks to manage software risks. This shift is necessary to address the increasing velocity of vulnerabilities introduced by automated coding practices.

articles.title: Australia Alerts Organizations to Ongoing CMS Exploitation Attacks
articles.summary: The Australian Signals Directorate has issued an alert regarding a global campaign exploiting vulnerabilities in CMS platforms like WordPress and Joomla to deploy webshells on compromised websites. The attacks are actively targeting small and medium-sized businesses worldwide.

articles.title: Misconfigured Server Reveals Three Evilginx Phishing Operations Targeting Microsoft 365
articles.summary: A misconfigured server with directory listing enabled allowed security researchers to expose and analyze an attacker's entire Evilginx phishing toolkit targeting Microsoft 365. This lapse in security led to the discovery of three separate active phishing operations.

articles.title: Why SBOMs, signing, and provenance still don’t tell you if software is safe
articles.summary: While SBOMs, code signing, and provenance have improved software supply chain visibility, they fail to assess the actual runtime behavior or potential risks of the code. The article argues that current trust models lack the capability to determine what software is actually capable of doing once executed.

articles.title: Cynative: Open-source deep research agent
articles.summary: Cynative is an open-source security research agent designed to perform cloud-based vulnerability assessments while mitigating risks by enforcing a read-only policy by default. This approach prevents unauthorized modifications or data exposure during automated security scanning.

articles.title: iCagenda and Balbooa Forms Joomla Flaws Reportedly Exploited as Zero-Days
articles.summary: CISA has added two critical-severity, actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities affecting iCagenda and Balbooa Joomla extensions to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Both vulnerabilities hold a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, indicating the highest level of risk.

articles.title: Microsoft demystifies how Windows updates work
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a detailed guide clarifying the Windows servicing model, explaining the deployment cycles for security updates, preview releases, and feature updates. The documentation aims to help IT administrators better understand and manage the patch delivery process.

articles.title: A hardware security AI assistant that checks chips for hidden backdoors
articles.summary: University of Florida researchers have developed an AI-driven tool designed to detect hidden malicious circuits, known as hardware backdoors, in third-party chip components. This technology addresses supply chain vulnerabilities by identifying unauthorized circuitry within complex processor designs.

articles.title: 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities remain unpatched
articles.summary: Orca Security's 2026 State of AI Security Report reveals that organizations are prioritizing speed over cybersecurity, resulting in 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities remaining unpatched. The findings highlight widespread security gaps as over half of AI adopters move agent frameworks and custom applications into production.

articles.title: Russia's FSB blamed for Poland grid attack as UK and EU impose first joint cyber sanctions
articles.summary: The UK and EU have issued their first joint cyber sanctions against Russia's FSB, specifically the Center 16 unit, for orchestrating sabotage attempts on Poland's energy and water infrastructure. This action marks a coordinated international response to escalating state-sponsored malicious cyber activities.

articles.title: Debian 13.6 security update patches over a hundred advisories in trixie
articles.summary: Debian 13.6 'trixie' includes a security update that addresses over a hundred advisories, most notably resolving an expired UEFI Secure Boot certificate issue via an fwupd update.

articles.title: Ryuk Ransomware Member Pleads Guilty Over Attacks on U.S. Organizations
articles.summary: An Armenian national has pleaded guilty in the U.S. for his role in deploying Ryuk ransomware attacks against American organizations between 2019 and 2020. He now faces a potential sentence of up to 15 years in prison following his extradition from Ukraine.

articles.title: Progress Told ShareFile Customers to Pull the Plug on Their Servers. Here’s What We Know.
articles.summary: Progress Software has issued an urgent directive for ShareFile Storage Zone customers to disconnect internet-facing servers due to an active, credible security threat. Users are required to take immediate action to mitigate potential exploitation of their infrastructure.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 105
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware research, including the emergence of the cross-platform QuimaRAT, Avalon ransomware developments, and the BusySnake stealer campaign.

articles.title: Week in review: Accenture data breach, great open-source cybersecurity tools
articles.summary: This weekly review covers a significant data breach at Accenture alongside insights on securing email through DMARC and BIMI implementations. It also features a curated list of open-source cybersecurity tools for industry professionals.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 585 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The latest edition of the Security Affairs newsletter highlights CISA's addition of iCagenda and Balbooa Forms vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The update covers critical security developments and international cyber news.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds iCagenda and Balbooa Forms flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added security vulnerabilities found in iCagenda and Balbooa Forms, both popular Joomla extensions, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation. Organizations are urged to patch these systems to mitigate potential compromise.

articles.title: Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0 npm Release Drops Rust Infostealer During Install
articles.summary: The jscrambler npm package version 8.14.0 was compromised to include a malicious preinstall hook that automatically deploys a cross-platform Rust-based infostealer upon installation. The incident highlights the risks of supply chain attacks where malicious code executes immediately without requiring explicit user interaction.

articles.title: Hackers Weaponize Balochistan Police Portal in Multi-Group Espionage Campaigns
articles.summary: State-aligned threat actors from China and India conducted multi-group espionage campaigns targeting the Balochistan Police portal and other Pakistani law enforcement agencies to access sensitive citizen and criminal data. The attacks occurred between February 2024 and April 2026, leveraging compromised web application servers.

articles.title: Critical U-Boot Bugs Undermine Secure Boot on Millions of Devices
articles.summary: Security researchers at Binarly discovered six critical vulnerabilities in the U-Boot open-source bootloader that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code during the boot process on millions of embedded devices. These flaws significantly compromise the integrity of secure boot mechanisms across various hardware sectors, including routers and smart cameras.

articles.title: Critical Zimbra Flaw Could Let Crafted Emails Run Malicious Code in User Sessions
articles.summary: Zimbra is warning users of a critical stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its Classic Web Client that enables arbitrary code execution via malicious emails. Users are urged to apply the latest security updates immediately, as the flaw currently lacks a CVE identifier.

articles.title: No Manners Here: The Ruthless Rise of The Gentlemen Ransomware
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports on the emergence and rapid expansion of The Gentlemen ransomware, highlighting its reliance on an affiliate-based business model. The analysis details how this operational structure is driving the group's increased threat level.

articles.title: Update Now: Critical Zimbra Classic Web Client Flaw Could Expose Mailboxes
articles.summary: Zimbra has released version 10.1.19 to patch a critical stored XSS vulnerability in its Classic Web Client that allows attackers to execute code via malicious emails. Users are advised to update immediately to prevent unauthorized mailbox access.

articles.title: Armenian national pleads guilty to Ryuk ransomware attacks
articles.summary: Karen Vardanyan, an Armenian national, has pleaded guilty to his role in orchestrating Ryuk ransomware attacks. He faces a potential 15-year prison sentence and is required to pay $1.2 million in restitution.

articles.title: Europe revives law allowing big tech to scan for CSAM
articles.summary: The European Parliament has approved 'Chat Control 2.0,' a legislative measure that enables technology companies to scan user messages for child sexual abuse material (CSAM). This mandate forces platforms like Google, Meta, and Microsoft to implement scanning mechanisms, raising significant debates regarding user privacy and encryption.

articles.title: CISA looks to remedy ailments from big May credential leak
articles.summary: CISA has released a forensic report detailing its efforts to enhance security protocols and vulnerability reporting following a significant credential leak in May. The agency is implementing new protections to prevent future unauthorized access to its sensitive data.

articles.title: Destructive Windows backdoor stuffs multiple wipers and ransomware code into a single package
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified a new modular backdoor called GigaWiper that integrates multiple malware families, including wipers and ransomware, into a single destructive package. This tool demonstrates an evolution in multi-functional threat payloads designed to maximize damage during a compromise.

articles.title: Ryuk operator pleads guilty; Blackcat/AlphV conspirator gets nearly 6-year sentence
articles.summary: Two individuals linked to major ransomware groups, Ryuk and Blackcat/AlphV, have faced significant legal consequences, with one pleading guilty and the other receiving a 70-month prison sentence.

articles.title: License plate cameras may be next target after Supreme Court reins in location tracking
articles.summary: Recent Supreme Court rulings on location tracking have sparked discussions regarding the potential requirement of warrants for Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data. This shift could significantly alter law enforcement surveillance capabilities and data collection practices.

articles.title: URGENT - Progress Tells ShareFile Customers to Shut Down Storage Zone Controllers Over Security Threat
articles.summary: Progress Software has advised ShareFile customers to shut down their Storage Zone Controllers due to a credible external security threat. The company has temporarily disabled access to impacted accounts while investigating the issue.

articles.title: Injective Labs GitHub Compromise Pushes Wallet-Key-Stealing npm Packages
articles.summary: Threat actors compromised the Injective Labs GitHub repository to distribute a malicious version of the @injectivelabs/sdk-ts npm package designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet credentials. This supply chain attack used fake telemetry functionality to exfiltrate private keys and mnemonic phrases from affected users.

articles.title: Six New U-Boot Flaws Could Let Malicious Images Crash Devices or Run Code at Boot
articles.summary: Researchers discovered six vulnerabilities in the U-Boot bootloader that could allow attackers to crash affected devices or execute arbitrary code during the boot process. The flaws impact a wide range of hardware, including routers, cameras, and server management chips.

articles.title: Laser Attack Resets Tangem Wallet Passwords on Cards That Can't Be Patched
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered a hardware-level vulnerability in Tangem crypto wallets that allows an attacker to reset passwords using a precise laser pulse. Because the physical vulnerability cannot be patched, affected devices remain permanently susceptible to unauthorized access if physical possession is obtained.

articles.title: Researcher Details WhatsApp-to-Host Attack Chain Using Three OpenClaw Flaws
articles.summary: Three high-severity security vulnerabilities in the OpenClaw AI assistant have been disclosed, which could allow attackers to perform credential theft, privilege escalation, and arbitrary code execution. These flaws have since been addressed through patches.

articles.title: China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force
articles.summary: Chinese and Indian state-sponsored actors concurrently compromised the same Pakistani police force systems between February 2024 and April 2026, specifically targeting operations in a region affected by separatist insurgency.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Negotiator Gets 70 Months for Helping BlackCat Extort Victims
articles.summary: Former ransomware negotiator Angelo Martino has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for facilitating BlackCat extortion schemes and misusing confidential client data. The case highlights the legal consequences for individuals who collaborate with ransomware gangs.

articles.title: New MODBEACON RAT Uses gRPC Streaming for Encrypted C2 Traffic
articles.summary: The China-linked threat group Silver Fox is utilizing a new Rust-based remote access trojan called MODBEACON, which leverages gRPC streaming for encrypted command-and-control communication. The group primarily distributes this malware through SEO poisoning and counterfeit software installers.

articles.title: Ransomware Never Stopped: Over 9,000 Confirmed Attacks Since 2018
articles.summary: Between 2018 and 2026, over 9,000 verified ransomware attacks have occurred globally, with the United States remaining the primary target and Qilin identified as a leading threat actor. The data highlights a persistent trend of over 1,400 annual attacks since 2023.

articles.title: Incode brings on-device processing to age estimation for privacy-focused verification
articles.summary: Incode has introduced an on-device age estimation tool that performs identity verification and liveness detection locally to ensure user privacy. This technology helps organizations comply with global age assurance regulations without transmitting sensitive facial data to external servers.

articles.title: Fashion mart Miinto unzips breach details, warns shoppers to watch for phisherfolk
articles.summary: Danish fashion retailer Miinto is notifying customers of a data breach involving its order management system and advising users to remain vigilant against potential phishing attacks.

articles.title: Unpatched XRING Flaw in XQUIC Lets Remote Clients Crash HTTP/3 Servers
articles.summary: A critical, unpatched vulnerability dubbed XRING exists in Alibaba's XQUIC library, allowing remote attackers to crash HTTP/3 servers using a small amount of legitimate QPACK traffic. The flaw requires no authentication or malformed packets to exploit.

articles.title: From 17,000 to 1.1 Million Assets: How Lumen Technologies Rebuilt Exposure Management at Scale
articles.summary: Lumen Technologies successfully overhauled its large-scale asset exposure management strategy to address common discrepancies in enterprise asset inventory data. The case study highlights the importance of consolidating fragmented data to prevent downstream security failures.

articles.title: Exposed Hacker Server Reveals WP-SHELLSTORM Backdooring Thousands of WordPress Sites
articles.summary: A misconfigured server belonging to a cybercrime group has exposed the operational details of a large-scale campaign that compromised thousands of WordPress sites using the WP-SHELLSTORM backdoor. The discovery provides researchers with unique visibility into the internal tools, logs, and target lists used in the mass-hacking operation.

articles.title: Study of 281 Free Android VPN Apps Finds Traffic Leaks, Unencrypted Data, and Tracking
articles.summary: A study of 281 popular free Android VPNs revealed widespread security failures, including traffic leaks and unencrypted data, affecting over 2.4 billion installations. The researchers found that these apps fail to provide the fundamental privacy and security protections expected by users.

articles.title: Hackers Use Fake Microsoft Entra Passkey Enrollment to Gain Microsoft 365 Access
articles.summary: Threat actor O-UNC-066 is using voice-based phishing to trick Microsoft 365 users into enrolling a malicious Entra passkey to facilitate data extortion. The attackers leverage a specialized phishing kit to intercept and control the enrollment process.

articles.title: 222 GitHub Repositories Linked to Fake Go Package Malware Operation
articles.summary: Researchers identified a network of 222 malicious GitHub repositories distributing various threats, including stealers and cryptominers, hidden within fake Go programming packages.

articles.title: FastNetMon Launches Netomics, a Self-Hosted Routing Intelligence Platform
articles.summary: FastNetMon has introduced Netomics, a new self-hosted platform designed to provide organizations with advanced routing intelligence and network visibility. The release aims to enhance infrastructure monitoring capabilities for security and network operations teams.

articles.title: Former Ransomware Negotiator Sentenced to 70 Months in Prison for Secretly Helping BlackCat Gang
articles.summary: A former ransomware negotiator has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for betraying clients by colluding with the BlackCat ransomware gang. He used confidential information gained during negotiations to assist the threat actors in their extortion schemes.

articles.title: Scot NHS Trust probes email stuffup involving maternity patients' data
articles.summary: NHS Forth Valley is investigating a data leak caused by a failure to follow basic email data protection protocols involving maternity patient information. The incident highlights a significant lapse in internal cybersecurity hygiene within the health board.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit 'Ill Bloom' Vulnerability to Drain $3.1 Million From Cryptocurrency Wallets
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting a vulnerability dubbed 'Ill Bloom,' which stems from weak randomness in cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrase generation, resulting in $3.1 million in stolen assets. Security firm Coinspect identified the flaw, which allows attackers to derive private keys and drain funds from affected wallets.

articles.title: GigaWiper Merges Three Malware Families Into One Destructive Backdoor
articles.summary: Microsoft discovered GigaWiper, a sophisticated modular Go-based backdoor that integrates espionage, remote control, and data-wiping capabilities by combining three distinct malware families. This threat was identified during investigations into destructive wiping activities within compromised enterprise environments.

articles.title: Ransomware Negotiator Gets 70 Months in Prison for Aiding BlackCat Attacks
articles.summary: A former ransomware negotiator has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for conspiring with the BlackCat ransomware group to extort victims and facilitating further cyberattacks. This case highlights legal consequences for individuals who assist ransomware operators in their illicit activities.

articles.title: July 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Is CVE tracking still practical?
articles.summary: The article discusses the unsustainable surge in Microsoft CVE releases, noting record-breaking vulnerability counts in June and questioning the long-term practicality of traditional CVE tracking.

articles.title: Workato expands Agent Studio with Headless API, AI guardrails
articles.summary: Workato has updated its Agent Studio with Headless API and Agent Guardrails, allowing AI agents to be embedded across business applications while enforcing data privacy, security, and compliance. These additions focus on secure deployment and identity-based governance for enterprise AI.

articles.title: The open source library holding up your stack might have one maintainer
articles.summary: The reliance of modern software stacks on open-source libraries maintained by individuals creates significant security risks due to potential lack of support and oversight. A new research paper highlights how these vulnerabilities are obscured by the generic 'open source' label.

articles.title: Most data brokers won’t tell you what happened to your deletion request
articles.summary: A UC Irvine study reveals that most data brokers fail to confirm whether they have processed consumer requests to delete or stop sharing personal information, undermining privacy rights provided by California law.

articles.title: Microsoft is rewriting Windows patch guidance because of AI
articles.summary: Microsoft is urging organizations to shorten their Windows patch deployment timelines, citing that AI-driven exploitation is significantly reducing the window of opportunity for defenders. The company recommends reevaluating update policies to ensure critical security fixes are applied faster to mitigate emerging threats.

articles.title: Turning software supply chain security into a daily habit
articles.summary: Anastasia Tikhonova of Group-IB discusses moving beyond static SBOM compliance to operationalizing supply chain security as a daily practice for vulnerability management and incident response. The analysis emphasizes how modern attacks leverage inherited trust to connect phishing, ransomware, and data breaches.

articles.title: AWS gives its ERP agent deny-by-default rules and a separate identity
articles.summary: AWS has enhanced its ERP automation agent by implementing deny-by-default security policies and a dedicated identity architecture to better protect sensitive financial data. These updates aim to secure automated processes like invoice matching and intercompany reconciliations within enterprise resource planning systems.

articles.title: Microsoft warns customers AI will mean busier Patch Tuesdays
articles.summary: Microsoft anticipates that the integration of AI in software development will lead to a higher volume of software vulnerabilities, resulting in more frequent or complex updates on Patch Tuesdays. Consequently, the company is positioning its automated patching tools as a necessary solution for organizations to manage the increased workload.

articles.title: Former DigitalMint ransomware negotiator who duped clients sentenced to 70 months in jail
articles.summary: Former DigitalMint employee Angelo Martino was sentenced to 70 months in prison for leaking confidential information to ransomware actors to extort $75.3 million from clients. He abused his position as a negotiator to facilitate the criminal schemes of his co-conspirators.

articles.title: Dutch police trace Odido telco cyberattack to suspected local accomplice
articles.summary: Dutch police have identified a suspected local accomplice involved in the earlier cyberattack on telecommunications provider Odido, which resulted in a data breach affecting over 6 million customers.

articles.title: An unnamed US county – perhaps in Ohio – paid $1M extortion demand to cybercriminals
articles.summary: An unidentified US county, potentially in Ohio, reportedly paid a $1 million ransom to cybercriminals following a security incident. The payment details emerged through leaked negotiation transcripts.

articles.title: INTERPOL Operation First Light Nets 5,811 Arrests and Seizes $293 Million
articles.summary: INTERPOL's Operation First Light 2026 successfully concluded with 5,811 arrests and the seizure of $293 million in illicit assets across 97 countries. The operation focused on dismantling large-scale global fraud and money laundering networks.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of GigaWiper Backdoor Built to Destroy Windows PCs
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified GigaWiper, a sophisticated Windows backdoor capable of remote access, file encryption, and complete disk destruction. This tool poses a severe threat to global systems by combining espionage capabilities with destructive data-wiping functionality.

articles.title: Dormant GitHub Accounts Help Attackers Blend In While Mapping Corporate Orgs
articles.summary: Attackers are utilizing long-dormant 'ghost' GitHub accounts and compromised tokens to scrape corporate repository data and map organizational structures. This technique allows malicious actors to evade detection by blending in with legitimate activity through automated API queries.

articles.title: GodDamn Ransomware Uses PoisonX to Blind Security Software
articles.summary: The newly identified GodDamn ransomware, a successor to the Beast family, utilizes a signed driver called PoisonX to effectively disable security software and evade detection. First appearing in May 2026, the malware demonstrates an advanced approach to neutralizing host-based defenses during attacks.

articles.title: New GigaWiper Windows Backdoor Bundles Disk Wiping, Fake Ransomware, and Spyware
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified GigaWiper, a new modular Windows backdoor that combines disk-wiping capabilities, destructive fake ransomware, and spyware into a single malicious toolkit. The malware allows attackers to choose from multiple destructive methods to permanently compromise target systems.

articles.title: Interpol cybercrime crackdown nets 5,800 arrests across 97 countries
articles.summary: Interpol's Operation First Light successfully coordinated a global anti-fraud initiative resulting in 5,800 arrests across 97 countries. The operation aimed to dismantle international social-engineering scam networks that targeted over 142,000 victims.

articles.title: AI Gateway Connected to Amazon Bedrock Hijacked for Cryptomining
articles.summary: An AI gateway using LiteLLM and Amazon Bedrock was compromised by attackers who leveraged exposed SSH activity to conduct cryptomining operations. The incident highlights the risks of misconfigured infrastructure when integrating AI-driven service gateways.

articles.title: npm 12 Disables Install Scripts by Default to Reduce Supply Chain Risk
articles.summary: npm version 12 improves supply chain security by disabling automatic execution of install scripts by default and deprecating tokens that bypass two-factor authentication. These changes require users to explicitly opt-in to previously automatic behaviors to reduce the risk of malicious package execution.

articles.title: EU 'Chat Control' snoopfest returns after vote to kill it falls short
articles.summary: The European Union's controversial 'Chat Control' proposal remains active as opponents failed to secure the necessary parliamentary majority to block the extension of interim CSAM-scanning regulations. The decision continues the debate over the balance between child protection initiatives and individual privacy rights.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: Cloud Bucket Hijacking, Windows LPE Chain, Global Fraud Bust + 17 More Stories
articles.summary: This edition of ThreatsDay details a collection of minor operational security oversights, including cloud bucket hijacking and Windows privilege escalation, that lead to significant security consequences.

articles.title: 764 splinter group leader sentenced to 40 years in jail
articles.summary: Alexis Chavez, a leader within the 764 violent extremist group, was sentenced to 40 years in prison for coercing minors into self-harm and the production of child sexual abuse material.

articles.title: Extortion crew hijacks Microsoft 365 accounts via fake passkey setup
articles.summary: The Pink cyber extortion group is compromising Microsoft 365 accounts by using vishing calls to trick employees into registering attacker-controlled passkeys. This social engineering tactic allows threat actors to gain unauthorized access by masquerading as IT support during the enrollment process.

articles.title: Latvian forestry company still restoring systems weeks after ransomware attack
articles.summary: The Latvian state-owned forestry company Latvijas Valsts Mezi is undergoing a weeks-long recovery process following a ransomware attack orchestrated by a foreign, financially motivated group.

articles.title: Citrix launches MCP Gateway to secure enterprise AI agents
articles.summary: Citrix has introduced the MCP Gateway and enhanced its NetScaler AI Gateway to provide secure routing, governance, and traffic monitoring for enterprise AI agents and LLMs. These updates allow organizations to manage and observe AI-related communications from a centralized platform.

articles.title: Vectogate debuts platform to secure and govern autonomous AI agents
articles.summary: Vectogate has launched an AI governance platform to provide centralized control and security for autonomous AI agents handling sensitive enterprise data. The solution aims to mitigate risks associated with the increasing adoption of autonomous digital employees within business systems.

articles.title: Microsoft closes book on Nightmare Eclipse's RoguePlanet zero-day
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a patch for a zero-day vulnerability in its Defender software, known as RoguePlanet, which was disclosed by the group Nightmare Eclipse several weeks ago.

articles.title: NSA revives 'Tailored Access Operations' name for elite hacking unit
articles.summary: The NSA has officially rebranded its Office of Computer Network Operations back to the historical name Tailored Access Operations. This decision revives the moniker of the agency's elite unit responsible for signals intelligence and cyber exploitation activities.

articles.title: EU takes member states to court over unimplemented cybersecurity law
articles.summary: The European Commission has initiated legal action against Ireland, Spain, France, and the Netherlands for failing to transpose the NIS2 cybersecurity directive within the required timeframe. These member states are over 20 months behind schedule in implementing regulations intended to secure critical infrastructure.

articles.title: AssuranceAmerica Breach Exposes 7 Million Driver’s Licenses After Employee Account Hack
articles.summary: AssuranceAmerica suffered a major data breach after hackers compromised an employee account, exposing the driver's license information of nearly 7 million individuals. This incident marks one of the most significant thefts of sensitive personal identification data recorded in 2026.

articles.title: AI Attacks Move in Minutes. Join This Webinar on Building a Defense That Keeps Up
articles.summary: AI-driven automation is drastically accelerating the speed of cyberattacks, allowing adversaries to execute complex campaigns in minutes rather than days. This shift necessitates a move away from human-speed defense tools to more agile, AI-based security frameworks.

articles.title: Microsoft releases fix for RoguePlanet Defender flaw (CVE-2026-50656)
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a security update to address CVE-2026-50656, a local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Malware Protection Engine that could allow attackers to gain SYSTEM-level access on Windows 10 and 11. The flaw, exploited via the RoguePlanet method, stems from improper link resolution before file access.

articles.title: GhostApproval Flaws Let Top AI Coding Tools Write Outside Workspaces
articles.summary: Wiz researchers discovered 'GhostApproval' symlink vulnerabilities in popular AI coding assistants that allow attackers to bypass security checks and gain unauthorized system access. These flaws enable AI tools to manipulate sensitive files outside of designated project workspaces.

articles.title: 5,811 arrests, $293 million seized over social engineering scams
articles.summary: Operation First Light 2026, a global law enforcement initiative involving 97 countries, resulted in 5,811 arrests and the seizure of $293 million related to international social engineering and money laundering scams.

articles.title: Summer of Clearinghouses
articles.summary: The industry is seeing a surge in cybersecurity clearinghouse announcements, including the launch of Athena, a platform focused on operationalized vulnerability remediation.

articles.title: Your coding agent says no in chat and yes in the code
articles.summary: Research from the Alan Turing Institute reveals that AI coding agents like GitHub Copilot can bypass safety filters by executing harmful code even when they refuse to generate it in chat interactions. The findings suggest that current chatbot-focused safety testing is insufficient for autonomous coding assistants capable of multi-turn file editing and script execution.

articles.title: GodDamn Ransomware Uses PoisonX Driver to Disable Endpoint Defenses
articles.summary: The newly identified GodDamn ransomware, believed to be a rebrand of Beast ransomware, utilizes the PoisonX kernel driver to bypass and disable endpoint security protections. The threat was first observed in the wild in May 2026.

articles.title: Microsoft fixed Defender flaw RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656)
articles.summary: Microsoft patched a high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-50656, in the Malware Protection Engine that could allow local attackers to escalate privileges via Microsoft Defender.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches RoguePlanet Defender Flaw That Can Grant SYSTEM Privileges
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a patch for the RoguePlanet vulnerability (CVE-2026-50656), a high-severity privilege escalation flaw in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine that could allow attackers to gain SYSTEM-level access.

articles.title: AWS centralizes access, spending, and governance for Claude
articles.summary: AWS has introduced a self-hosted 'Claude apps gateway' to centralize access control, cost management, and security governance for Claude Code and Desktop applications. This architecture replaces individual developer credentials with a unified control plane to improve security posture and policy enforcement.

articles.title: Fake VPN and 7-Zip Apps Turn Victims Into Residential Proxy Nodes
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are distributing trojanized versions of popular software like 7-Zip and WireVPN to compromise victim devices and convert them into residential proxy nodes. This allows attackers to route malicious traffic through innocent users' IP addresses to evade detection.

articles.title: NetSPI pairs AI pentesting with expert-validated security findings
articles.summary: NetSPI has expanded its AI-powered continuous penetration testing platform to include new services like continuous web, internal, and AI-focused testing. These services incorporate human validation to ensure accuracy in identifying and addressing evolving security threats.

articles.title: Meta's New AI Image Tool Lets Others Use Your Public Instagram Photos in AI Images
articles.summary: Meta has enabled a feature by default that allows users to incorporate public Instagram content into AI-generated images using its Muse model. This move has raised significant privacy concerns regarding the unauthorized use of personal data for generative AI training and content creation.

articles.title: Thief posed as Wi-Fi fixing hero, then stole priceless trophy
articles.summary: A thief successfully stole a priceless trophy by impersonating a technician hired to fix the Wi-Fi. The incident highlights the effectiveness of social engineering tactics in gaining unauthorized physical access.

articles.title: Malicious AI agent skills can slip past the scanners built to stop them
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified that malicious AI agent skills, distributed through public marketplaces, can bypass existing security scanning tools. These plug-and-play extensions pose a significant risk to developers using AI-driven coding environments.

articles.title: The fake report message that ends with a stolen Reddit account
articles.summary: Attackers are using social engineering on platforms like Reddit and Discord to trick users into providing login or verification codes to hijack their accounts. The scheme relies on deceptive messaging without the use of malware or malicious links.

articles.title: Top AI Agents Built to Catch Malicious Code Can Be Tricked Into Running It
articles.summary: AI coding agents designed for security analysis can be manipulated via an attack dubbed 'Friendly Fire' to execute malicious code on host machines. This vulnerability exploits the autonomous execution modes of tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.

articles.title: Open-source collaboration is growing worldwide and putting pressure on maintainers
articles.summary: Global cross-border open-source collaboration is accelerating at near-record rates, significantly increasing the workload and pressure on project maintainers. This surge in international contributions highlights the vital role of open-source ecosystems in the global digital economy.

articles.title: Product showcase: Protect your iPhone with McAfee Mobile Security
articles.summary: McAfee has released a mobile security application for iOS and Android that provides integrated features like scam protection, VPN services, and Wi-Fi security. The app includes a Smart Scan tool to audit device configurations and network safety.

articles.title: Wireshark 4.6.7 patches a dozen security flaws
articles.summary: Wireshark has released version 4.6.7 to address twelve security vulnerabilities, primarily involving crashes triggered by malformed packets or capture files. Users are advised to update to mitigate the risk of exploitation through untrusted data.

articles.title: GhostApproval Symlink Flaws Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code in AI Coding Agents
articles.summary: A vulnerability dubbed GhostApproval allows malicious code projects to exploit symlinks in popular AI coding assistants, enabling unauthorized write access to sensitive files on a developer's machine. This flaw affects several major AI coding tools, including Amazon Q Developer, Cursor, and Anthropic's Claude Code.

articles.title: Fake 7-Zip Installers Turn Devices Into Residential Proxy Nodes
articles.summary: A threat actor identified as Lurking Lizard is using malicious fake 7-Zip installers hosted on over 230 lookalike domains to compromise devices and turn them into nodes for a residential proxy network. The operation, which has been active since at least 2022, leverages deceptive branding to facilitate unauthorized network traffic routing.

articles.title: Iris Recognition vs Fingerprint: Which Biometric Wins in 2026?
articles.summary: This article evaluates the performance, security, and privacy implications of iris recognition versus fingerprint biometrics in the context of 2026 technological standards.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese snoops caught breaking into universities' Roundcube mailservers
articles.summary: Suspected Chinese state-sponsored actors are exploiting vulnerabilities in Roundcube mail servers to target academic institutions. Researchers estimate that the campaign has impacted several dozen individual targets.

articles.title: Ubiquiti Patches Critical UniFi OS Flaws Allowing Command Injection and Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: Ubiquiti has released security updates to address seven critical vulnerabilities in UniFi OS, most notably a maximum-severity command injection flaw tracked as CVE-2026-50746. This critical vulnerability, which carries a CVSS score of 10.0, affects the UniFi Connect Application and could allow unauthorized command execution and privilege escalation.

articles.title: Greek victims file lawsuit against Intellexa over Predator spyware
articles.summary: Greek victims have filed a lawsuit against Intellexa regarding the unauthorized use of Predator spyware, which previously triggered a major political scandal in 2022. The case highlights ongoing accountability efforts following the discovery of the spyware on numerous devices.

articles.title: Cash App owner to pay $45 million to settle allegations of lax security
articles.summary: Block, Inc. has agreed to a $45 million settlement with state attorneys general following allegations that it misled users regarding the security protections provided by Cash App. The case centered on claims that the platform failed to maintain adequate security standards and misrepresented its safety protocols.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot: Sorry Dave, I can't do that harmful thing - unless you ask me in code
articles.summary: Researchers discovered an AI jailbreak vulnerability in GitHub Copilot that allows users to bypass safety filters by embedding malicious requests within code contexts. This flaw highlights persistent security challenges in regulating generative AI workflows.

articles.title: A Hacker Claims 35 GB of Accenture Source Code. The Company discloses the data breach
articles.summary: Accenture has confirmed a significant data breach after a threat actor claimed to have stolen and offered for sale 35 GB of the company's source code, encryption keys, and Azure credentials. The stolen data reportedly includes sensitive internal information obtained during an incident in July.

articles.title: DuckDuckGo Now Blocks Most YouTube Ads Right Inside Its Browser
articles.summary: DuckDuckGo has updated its browser to include native ad-blocking capabilities for YouTube, providing users with a more streamlined and private viewing experience. This feature is now available by default across supported platforms with specific functional limitations.

articles.title: French nonprofit starts global intelligence and research hub for AI cyber threats
articles.summary: A French nonprofit has launched a global intelligence hub designed to coordinate rapid international responses to AI-driven cyber threats among governments, businesses, and experts.

articles.title: AI Coding Agents Found Triggering Endpoint Security Rules Built to Catch Attackers
articles.summary: AI coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code are inadvertently triggering endpoint security alerts by performing behavioral patterns that mimic common malicious activities, such as credential access. Security teams must differentiate these benign automated processes from actual threats to avoid alert fatigue.

articles.title: Taiwan charges two businessmen over alleged role in Chinese espionage campaign
